candidate-11.title: Codex Vaticanus at the end of Mark

images.alt: Complete monochrome facsimile page of Codex Vaticanus page 1303: Mark ends after verse 8 in the second column, with a decorated ending and the third column left blank.

candidate-11.caption: Codex Vaticanus (GA 03/B), Vat. gr. 1209, facsimile page 1303. CSNTM tags this page to Mark 16:1–8. Mark ends after verse 8, and the remaining third column is blank.
candidate-11.demonstrates: This one witness's facsimile page ends Mark after 16:8 and preserves the physical page context at that point.
candidate-11.doesNotEstablish: It does not by itself establish Mark's original ending, the reading of another manuscript, or the distribution of endings across the manuscript tradition.
candidate-11.credit: Image via the Center for the Study of New Testament Manuscripts (CSNTM); manuscript held by the Biblioteca Apostolica Vaticana, Vat. gr. 1209.

candidate-17.title: Codex Bezae and the woman caught in adultery

images.alt: Complete Greek verso page of Codex Bezae, folio 133v, containing John 7:43 through 8:4; the account begins in the lower portion of the page.
Complete Greek verso page of Codex Bezae, folio 134v, containing John 8:5–17; the account continues from the top of the page.

candidate-17.caption: Codex Bezae (GA 05/D), Cambridge University Library MS Nn.2.41, Greek folios 133v and 134v. CSNTM tags the pages to John 7:43–8:4 and John 8:5–17, respectively; together they include John 7:53–8:11 in this location.
candidate-17.demonstrates: These two Greek pages show that this witness contains the passage between John 7:52 and 8:12.
candidate-17.doesNotEstablish: They do not by themselves establish that the passage was original to John, its reading or location in another witness, or its prevalence in the broader tradition.
candidate-17.credit: Cambridge University Library, MS Nn.2.41; images via CSNTM. Source images state Copyright Cambridge University Library and CC BY-NC 3.0.
candidate-17.reuseStatement: Used noncommercially in Ad Fontes NT under the source-image CC BY-NC 3.0 notice and the project owner's recorded 2026-09-12 authorization for this free educational web and offline desktop distribution.

candidate-26.title: Codex Sinaiticus at 1 Timothy 3:16

manuscript.name: Codex Sinaiticus
manuscript.locator: local folio 294b; column 2 line 47 through column 3 line 10

images.alt: Complete four-column facsimile page of Codex Sinaiticus folio 294b; 1 Timothy 3:16 begins at the bottom of column two and continues at the top of column three.

candidate-26.caption: Codex Sinaiticus (GA 01/א), British Library Add. 43725, folio 294b. CSNTM tags this page to 1 Timothy 2:12–4:16. The Codex Sinaiticus Project transcription records the first-hand reading ος ('who') at 3:16 and a later correction by corrector e to θεός ('God').
candidate-26.demonstrates: The page and primary transcription permit inspection of this witness's initial reading and its recorded later correction in their page context.
candidate-26.doesNotEstablish: They do not by themselves establish the autograph reading, the reading of Codex Alexandrinus or another witness, or the relative weight of the alternatives.
candidate-26.credit: Image via CSNTM from the J. T. and Zelma Luther Archives, A. Webb Roberts Library, Southwestern Baptist Theological Seminary; manuscript held by the British Library, Add. 43725. Transcription verification: Codex Sinaiticus Project.
candidate-26.reuseStatement: Used in Ad Fontes NT under the project owner's recorded 2026-09-12 authorization for this free educational web and offline desktop distribution; no broader reuse is granted by Ad Fontes NT.

candidate-27.title: Codex Sinaiticus at 1 John 5:7–8

images.alt: Complete four-column facsimile page of Codex Sinaiticus folio 324; 1 John 5:7–8 appears in the upper half of the first column.

candidate-27.caption: Codex Sinaiticus (GA 01/א), British Library Add. 43725, folio 324. CSNTM tags this page to 1 John 5:5–21. The Codex Sinaiticus Project transcription reads 'the three who testify: the Spirit and the water and the blood,' without the expanded Father, Word, and Holy Spirit clause.
candidate-27.demonstrates: The page and primary transcription show the shorter form of 1 John 5:7–8 in this one fourth-century witness.
candidate-27.doesNotEstablish: They do not by themselves establish the autograph reading, the origin or date of the expanded clause, its reading in another Greek or Latin witness, or its prevalence.
candidate-27.credit: Image via CSNTM from the J. T. and Zelma Luther Archives, A. Webb Roberts Library, Southwestern Baptist Theological Seminary; manuscript held by the British Library, Add. 43725. Transcription verification: Codex Sinaiticus Project.
